narratives.Description: deft update renders AGENTS.md from stale content while depositing newer templates, and stamps it with the new sha
narratives.Overview:
1. **Same-root AGENTS render on update.** In the `deft update` / `runRefreshDeposit` path, make `writeAgentsMd` read `templates/agents-entry.md` from the **same content tree** just reconciled for deposit (engine `resolveInstalledContentRoot()` result and/or post-copy `.deft/core` via explicit `readTemplate` / `readAgentsTemplateFromContentTree` / `agentsRefreshPlanWithInstalledTemplate` seams). Do **not** rely on bare `agentsRefreshPlan(projectDir, { frameworkRoot: deftDir })`, which still walks `contentRoot()` prefer-package and can hit a stale project `node_modules/@deftai/directive-content`.

2. **Stamp identity of the rendered tree.** Stamp managed-section `sha=` from that same tree's version (headless `collectAgentsMdFile` / `resolveSha: () => version` pattern). Frame P2 as stamp identity MUST equal the content tree used for the managed body in that write. Do not bind primary AC to the `agents:refresh` "unchanged - sha match" CLI phrase; that phrase is body-equality currentness after `stripManagedSectionAttrs`, not the attr stamp.

3. **Regression.** Add a fixture that installs divergent engine vs project content-package versions and asserts post-update AGENTS managed body matches deposited `.deft/core/templates/agents-entry.md`, with `sha=` from that same tree.

4. **Companion disclosure only.** `npm ci` / install-ordering messaging may accompany for remaining prefer-package readers (`agents:refresh` default path). It is not Prefer-A alone and must not be an alternate first-ship fix that leaves a green update able to commit deposit/AGENTS disagreement. If an "installed package is SoT" branch is kept, it must refuse or warn-fail the AGENTS write when engine content root and project prefer-package root diverge mid-update.

5. **Surfaces.** `packages/core/src/init-deposit/scaffold.ts` (`writeAgentsMd`); `packages/core/src/init-deposit/refresh.ts` (call site); reuse `#4706` helpers in doctor/content-root adjacent modules (`readAgentsTemplateFromContentTree` / `agentsRefreshPlanWithInstalledTemplate`); headless same-root pointer in `headless-manifest.ts` as the invariant exemplar; tests under init-deposit / content-root; CHANGELOG Unreleased.

6. **Non-goals.** Do not globally recut `contentRoot()` prefer-package (explicitly deferred by #4706). Do not expand into the #5011 clause:N id pattern. Do not redesign the full update dirty-tree / write-class ledger (#5096 class) beyond AGENTS render source + sha stamp consistency. Do not auto-ingest after ingest-ready.

## Current known state (2026-09-30 Stage A)

Stage A `task triage:evaluate -- 5013` on origin/master `fc1363287967`:

- validity: **still-open**
- WIP / open PRs / duplicates: none
- critique-recommend: false (before mechanism-shaped chip)
- sink: `.deft-scratch/issue-eval/fc1363287967/70228efc-d716-41c3-810d-b437a5c303c9`

### Live gap

`deft update` can deposit newer `.deft/core/templates/agents-entry.md` while rendering `AGENTS.md` from a stale installed content package in the same run, then stamp the managed section `sha=<new version>`. Staleness checks pass; consumers who commit the update ship a header that disagrees with the deposit and see unexplained AGENTS.md diffs on later ritual refreshes. Related ordering: `npm install` can leave disk content at the old pin while claiming the tree satisfies the new pin; `npm ci` is what actually replaces files.

Filed alongside #5011 from the same consumer update; independent of the clause:N id pattern.

### Spend recommendation

Concrete update write-set / AGENTS render + sha-stamp consistency defect with a named suggested fix (render from the just-written deposit, or stamp the content actually rendered and surface npm-ci ordering). Recommended Dual-stop **N=1**.

Operator bare `arc` / issue number under **#5111 defaults**: yolo + no-ingest + use recommended Dual-stop (no `n=` ask).

## Verdict

Stop 1 pains **P1** and **P2** name a real mid-update dual-root defect. The right bind shape is **same-root render + stamp identity of the tree actually rendered**, reusing mechanisms that already exist (headless same-root; #4706 explicit template-root bypass). An OR that lets "stamp what you rendered + tell the operator to `npm ci`" stand alone still leaves a successful `deft update` able to commit deposit templates that disagree with AGENTS.md.

## Re-verification at pin `fc1363287967413846934ecac824c2be1a6e6d51`

1. **Deposit source (engine resolve).** `runRefreshDeposit` resolves content via `resolveInstalledContentRoot()` (`import.meta.resolve` of `@deftai/directive-content/package.json` from the engine) and copies/reconciles that tree into `.deft/core` (`packages/core/src/init-deposit/refresh.ts`, `packages/core/src/deposit/resolve-content.ts`).

2. **AGENTS write path.** After deposit work, update calls `writeAgentsMd(projectDir, payloadReadRoot, ...)`. In normal (non-port-record) mode `recordModePayloadRoot` returns `deftDir` (`.deft/core`). `writeAgentsMd` then runs `agentsRefreshPlan(projectDir, { frameworkRoot: deftDir })` with **no** `readTemplate` / `resolveSha` seams (`packages/core/src/init-deposit/scaffold.ts`).

3. **Prefer-package hijack.** `agentsTemplatePath` does `join(contentRoot(frameworkRoot), "templates", "agents-entry.md")`. `contentRoot()` **prefers** an ancestor `node_modules/@deftai/directive-content` over the flattened deposit (`packages/core/src/content-root.ts`). Passing `frameworkRoot: deftDir` therefore does **not** guarantee reading the just-written deposit when the project still has an older content package on disk.

4. **False-fresh `sha=`.** With `frameworkRoot: deftDir`, `resolveFrameworkSha` -> `resolveInventoryFrameworkIdentity` reads `.deft/core/package.json` (just copied -> **new** version) while the managed body can come from the **stale** prefer-package tree. `attributeRenderManagedSection` stamps `sha=<that identity>` onto whatever body was rendered.

5. **`agents:refresh` "unchanged - sha match".** At this pin the CLI phrase is emitted only when plan `state === "current"`, and currentness is **body equality after `stripManagedSectionAttrs`** — it does **not** consult the managed-section `sha=` attribute (`packages/cli/src/agents-refresh.ts`, `agentsRefreshPlan`). The false-fresh stamp is still harmful for humans and for "version looks current" reasoning; the issue's "sha match while still rewriting" wording overfits the attr stamp to that CLI phrase.

6. **Existing same-root inventory (do not invent a third).**
   - Headless init already renders AGENTS from the **SAME** content root as the payload and stamps `resolveSha: () => version` from that root (`packages/core/src/init-deposit/headless-manifest.ts` `collectAgentsMdFile`).
   - #4706 already added `readAgentsTemplateFromContentTree` / `agentsRefreshPlanWithInstalledTemplate` so doctor can read an explicit content tree **without** walking `contentRoot()` prefer-package, and CHANGELOG records that #4706 **did not** recut prefer-package.
   - #4710 completed as pin/lock reconstitution, not as making walk-root canonical for AGENTS render.

Causal shape matching the filed consumer report: engine-resolved content (new) is deposited into `.deft/core`, while AGENTS render can prefer the project's still-stale `@deftai/directive-content` install; stamp follows deposit package.json. After `npm ci` aligns the project package, a later refresh rewrites the body to match the deposit.

## Findings

### 1. `blocks-the-design` — Prefer-A must require same-root AGENTS render (or fail-closed); npm-ci messaging is not a substitute

**Evidence.** Update already intends "render against `payloadReadRoot`/`deftDir`" (`writeAgentsMd(..., payloadReadRoot)`), but `contentRoot()` prefer-package can redirect the template read to a different physical tree than `resolveInstalledContentRoot()` used for the copy. Headless already forbids that drift; update does not reuse the invariant. The issue's OR admits a branch that only stamps the rendered identity and warns about `npm ci`.

**Failure mode.** A green `deft update` deposits newer `.deft/core/templates/agents-entry.md` and writes AGENTS.md from a stale project content package, stamped `sha=<new>`. Consumer commits the pair. Later ritual/`agents:refresh` after real package replace produces an unexplained AGENTS.md diff. Messaging `npm ci` after the fact does not prevent the disagreeing commit from the update that already succeeded.

**Disposition consequence.** Bound remedy must make the AGENTS template bytes come from the **same tree** update just reconciled for deposit (engine `resolveInstalledContentRoot` result and/or post-copy `deftDir` via explicit `readTemplate` / `readAgentsTemplateFromContentTree`, not bare `frameworkRoot: deftDir`). Stamp `sha=` from that same tree's version (headless pattern). `npm ci` / install-ordering disclosure may accompany for surfaces that still prefer-package (`agents:refresh` default path), but must not be Prefer-A alone. If the lean keeps an "installed package is SoT" branch, it must **refuse or warn-fail the AGENTS write** when engine content root and project prefer-package root diverge mid-update (#4706 already detects divergence for doctor).

### 2. `sharpens-framing` — P1 is right; state the dual resolver, not "deposit vs content package" alone

**Evidence.** Two resolvers: `resolveInstalledContentRoot` (engine module resolve) vs `contentRoot` ancestor prefer-package from `deftDir`. Tests document prefer-package over vendored deposit (`content-root.test.ts` hybrid npm-engine case).

**Failure mode.** A lean that only says "read deposit templates" without naming the prefer-package bypass can re-ship today's `frameworkRoot: deftDir` call and leave the bug.

**Disposition consequence.** Prefer-A / AC should cite explicit template-root seams (existing #4706 helpers or equivalent `readTemplate` + `resolveSha`) and a regression that installs divergent engine vs project content package versions and asserts update AGENTS body matches deposited `agents-entry.md`.

### 3. `sharpens-framing` — P2 keep false-fresh stamp; retarget the "sha match while rewriting" claim

**Evidence.** Managed-section `sha=` is inventory/framework identity at stamp time; `agents:refresh` no-op phrase is content-body currentness. They are different signals sharing the word "sha".

**Failure mode.** Binding P2 to "make agents:refresh stop saying sha match while rewriting" can miss the update-time false stamp, or chase CLI copy while leaving deposit/AGENTS disagreement.

**Disposition consequence.** Frame P2 as: stamp identity MUST equal the content tree used for the managed body in that write. Post-update `agents:refresh` body rewrite after package align is a symptom, not the primary gate. Optional footnote: rename/clarify deposit-sha vs managed-section `sha=` in docs later; out of first-ship if same-root+stamp bind holds.

### 4. `footnote` — Injection/swarm lens

Installer path selection and stamp consistency only; no new authority, envelope, or concurrency surface beyond existing AGENTS refresh lock (#1329). No injection finding.

### 5. `footnote` — Road not taken / steelman

**Road not taken:** Global recut of `contentRoot()` prefer-package (explicitly deferred by #4706). Larger blast across doctor/session/hashDepositTemplates; Stop 1 non-goals already keep this off the dirty-tree/#5096 ledger expansion. Local same-root bind at update/init `writeAgentsMd` is enough for this issue.

**Steelman of stamp+npm-ci-only:** If project `node_modules` were the sole intentional SoT, stamping that tree's version and requiring `npm ci` before trusting AGENTS would be coherent. Flip condition: update must not deposit a **newer** engine content tree beside an AGENTS body from a different tree in the same successful run. Today's copy-from-engine + prefer-package-render violates that; hence same-root (or refuse) wins.

## Bind shape (critic recommendation)

Prefer-A: **same-root render** (reuse headless + #4706 explicit template root) **and** stamp from that root's version. Treat npm-ci ordering as companion disclosure for remaining prefer-package readers, not an alternate first-ship fix.

## In plain English

`deft update` can deposit a new content tree into `.deft/core` while AGENTS.md is still rendered through `contentRoot()` prefer-package from a stale project install, then stamp `sha=` from the deposit package.json. That dual-root path is the real defect. The bind is same-root render plus stamp identity of the tree actually rendered, reusing headless same-root and the #4706 explicit template-root helpers. An OR that only stamps and tells the operator to run `npm ci` is not Prefer-A. Confirming this map means the Bound remedy list is the build contract. The same parent wrote Stop 1 5914043979. Critic 5914153317 checks the findings. Whether the list covers the two pains stays open until a later critic targets those cites.

**Lean:** open critique. This map is the bind.

metadata.issueBody:
Second, separate defect found in the same update, on the same consumer (`3Ci-Consulting/kantata-mcp`, 0.119.2 → 0.119.8, darwin / node 24).

**`deft update` deposits templates and renders AGENTS.md from something else, in the same run.**

After `deft update --yes`, the deposited templates and the header it wrote beside them disagreed:

| | `directive doctor --full` | #4821 envelope wording | `project:write-narratives` ⊗ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.deft/core/templates/agents-entry.md` (just deposited) | present | present | present |
| `AGENTS.md` (rendered in the same run) | absent — rendered `directive doctor` | absent | absent |

Running `deft agents:refresh` afterwards — once `npm ci` had brought `node_modules/@deftai/directive-content` to 0.119.8 — produced a header that matches the deposited templates, and repeated refreshes are a no-op. The mid-flight render was not stable: `agents:refresh` reported `unchanged - sha match` against it while still rewriting the body, because the stamp already said `sha=0.119.8`.

That last part is the sharp edge. The stale header carries a `sha=<new version>` stamp, so the staleness check passes and nothing flags it. A consumer who commits the update as-is ships a header that disagrees with its own deposit, and then sees an unexplained AGENTS.md diff at the start of every subsequent session that runs the ritual.

Suggested fix: render the managed section from the deposit that the same run just wrote, not from the installed content package — or, if the installed package is the intended source, have `deft update` say that `npm ci` is required before the header is correct, and make the sha stamp reflect the content actually rendered rather than the target version.

Related ordering note from the same update: `npm install` reported the tree as already satisfying the new pin while the files on disk were still 0.119.2. `npm ci` is what replaced them. If the header render does depend on the installed package, that combination means the default update path leaves a stale header silently.

Filed alongside #5011 (the `clause:N` id pattern), which came out of the same update but is independent.
